stages.label: Study
stages.description: A US bachelor’s degree typically takes four years.

stages.label: Post-study work visa
stages.description: Optional Practical Training (OPT) gives 12 months of work after graduation, up to 36 months for STEM degrees. Staying longer means winning the annual H-1B visa lottery.

stages.label: PR process
stages.description: There is no direct study-to-residence route. After H-1B an employer-sponsored green card runs about 3 to 4 years for most nationalities, but Indian and Chinese citizens face waits of a decade or more under per-country caps.

stages.label: Citizenship
stages.description: Green-card holders can apply for naturalization after five years of permanent residence.

sources.name: USCIS: Optional Practical Training (OPT) for F-1 students

stages.label: Study
stages.description: A Canadian bachelor's degree typically runs four years. Graduating from a program this length earns a post-graduation work permit (PGWP) valid for up to three years.

stages.label: Post-study work visa
stages.description: Express Entry's Canadian Experience Class needs 12 months of skilled Canadian work, gained on the PGWP, before you can apply for permanent residence.

stages.label: PR process
stages.description: After the work requirement is met, an Express Entry profile usually leads to an invitation and PR being granted within about a year. This duration is a representative estimate.

stages.label: Citizenship
stages.description: Citizenship needs 1,095 days (three years) of physical presence in the five years before applying. Time spent in Canada on the PGWP before PR counts as a half day each, up to 365 days.
